Vietnamese dining: a gentle introduction for visitors

From shared plates to street-food stalls, a few small customs make local meals more enjoyable.

7
Seven Travel Editorial TeamOctober 1, 2026 · 4 min read
THE JOURNAL

A better way to see Vietnam.

Explore at your pace with thoughtful local guidance.

Plan with confidence ↗
← More in Culture & Food

Eating is one of the best ways to connect with Vietnam. Meals can be lively, informal and built around sharing. Curiosity matters far more than mastering every custom.

Expect shared dishes

At many family-style meals, dishes are placed in the middle of the table. Take modest portions and watch how your hosts serve food, as customs vary by setting and region.

Street food with confidence

Look for busy stalls with food prepared fresh, and choose places that match your comfort level. If you have food allergies or dietary restrictions, communicate them clearly before ordering.

Be open to regional flavours

Dishes change from north to south. Even something familiar may be prepared differently in each region, which is part of the pleasure of travelling across Vietnam.
